headline: BREAKING: LOCALS PROTEST THE NEW MERIDIAN DATA CENTRE
body: Residents from the Polytechnic quarter have blockaded the service entrance. The organisers call it a peaceful occupation. The police call it a developing situation. A man in a hi-vis vest is trying to plug a kettle into the perimeter fence.

responses.label: Get Bramley behind the blockade
responses.hint: The protesters will love it. The candidate may not understand the word 'blockade'.
responses.flavour: Bramley appears on camera beside the protesters and says the data centre should be shut down immediately. Someone behind him is holding a sign that says NO MORE CLOUDS.

positionChange.position: Opposes the data centre and backs the blockade

responses.label: Condemn the violence and back the investment
responses.hint: A firm statement. Several people will agree with you.
responses.flavour: Bramley condemns the kettle incident and welcomes the jobs. The protesters boo the statement, then ask whether the jobs include catering.

positionChange.position: Supports the data centre and condemns the blockade

responses.label: Say nothing until the kettle situation is resolved
responses.hint: A holding statement is still technically a statement.
responses.flavour: Your office issues a statement saying you are monitoring the situation. The situation issues a statement saying it has not noticed.

headline: SERVICE INTERRUPTION: CAMPAIGN FEED PARTIALLY AVAILABLE
body: The local news site is returning incomplete pages. Polling data is missing. Your inbox shows three copies of the same message, each with a different timestamp. The campaign office phone rings once, displays a weather symbol, then stops.

responses.label: Wait for the systems to come back
responses.hint: The outage is affecting the whole district. Probably.
responses.flavour: You wait. The page reloads itself. For a moment the candidate's biography says he was born in 1842. Then it says 1971 again.

headline: SYSTEMS RESTORED; THREE RESIDENTS UNACCOUNTED FOR
body: The feeds return. The data centre is operating normally. The protest has dispersed, though nobody can locate the kettle, its owner, or the candidate's original statement. Bramley says he has always supported the centre and is surprised anyone remembers otherwise.

responses.label: Accept the clarification and move on
responses.hint: The clarification is 86 pages long and arrives in a leather folder.
responses.flavour: The campaign feed refreshes. Every poll now says 100%. Bramley insists this is what he meant all along.

positionChange.position: Enthusiastically supports the centre; denies ever opposing it

headline: THE ASHCOMBE HOUR WANTS YOUR CANDIDATE FOR A FULL HOUR
body: A local politics podcast with a startlingly large audience and a host who does actual research. An hour is a long time. Your candidate has not been interesting for an hour at any point in his life.

responses.label: Accept the invitation
responses.hint: An hour is a very long time to fill.
responses.flavour: You accept before you can think better of it. They record on Thursday. You have one afternoon to get him ready.

responses.label: Politely decline
responses.flavour: The host reads your decline statement aloud on air, slowly, in full, and then leaves a pause long enough to park a bus in.

headline: ONE AFTERNOON. WHAT DO YOU PREP HIM ON?
body: He will be asked about the railway, the hospital, and — because the host is good at this — his own record. You can only drill one thing properly.

responses.label: Railway policy, line by line
responses.hint: Dry, thorough, aimed squarely at the commute.
responses.flavour: He is word-perfect on the 07:42 and visibly bored by minute nine. The commuter forums call it 'the most substantial interview of the campaign', which is not a compliment about the campaign.

responses.label: Warmth, family, the personal story
responses.flavour: He talks about his father's allotment for eleven uninterrupted minutes. Two listeners write in to say they cried. One writes in to complain about the allotment waiting list.

responses.label: No prep. Let him be himself
responses.hint: Unfiltered. Could be electric. Could be a clip.
responses.flavour: He is loose, funny, and entirely unmanaged. Forty seconds of it are already a sound-on-loop with 200,000 views and a caption you would not have chosen.

headline: CANDIDATE PHOTOGRAPHED LEAVING CASINO AT 4AM
body: The Ashcombe Echo has a picture. In it, your candidate is squinting, holding a complimentary tote bag, and appears to be explaining something important to a bollard. The photographer has three more and is asking what they're worth.

responses.label: Deny everything
responses.flavour: You state that the candidate was at a constituency fundraiser. The Echo prints the photo next to your statement, which is the worst possible layout.

responses.label: Half-apology, full contrition tour
responses.flavour: The candidate is very sorry that people feel the way they do about the thing that did not technically happen.

responses.label: Bury it under a bigger story
responses.flavour: You leak a completely unrelated planning scandal to a rival paper. It works. It works so well that nobody can remember what your candidate stands for either.
